### Asia Gives Back the Huang Rally in a Morning, the Houthis Claim the Riyadh Tower and a Refinery at Ras Tanura, Tehran Counts Two More Tankers on Mines Against Four Crossings in the Visible Counter, and Moscow Files No Word on the Merkury Into a Fifth Day

Filed as: Edition No. 89 — The Overnight Watch · 2026-11-25T04:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-25-overnight-watch.html

The Night File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Asia Gives Back the Huang Rally in a Morning, the Houthis Claim the Riyadh Tower and a Refinery at Ras Tanura, Tehran Counts Two More Tankers on Mines Against Four Crossings in the Visible Counter, and Moscow Files No Word on the Merkury Into a Fifth Day

 The night file: a rally that crossed the Pacific on Monday and came back on Wednesday; a tariff file reopened in Washington while Washington slept; a claim from Sanaa that widens the Riyadh file to a refinery; a hundred and twelve drones counted over Ukraine; two more tankers claimed and none named; and a ministry’s silence entering its fifth day.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 0400 ET, Wednesday, November 25, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 88, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, from Edition No. 87, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Tuesday, in Edition No. 86, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Tuesday, and in Edition No. 85, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 on Tuesday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the overnight figures differ from the earlier figures, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Night in Brief: A Rally Returned, a Claim Widened, a Count Raised

The night’s largest movement ran backward. Asia, which leapt on Tuesday on Mr. Huang’s return to Nvidia—Seoul up about seven percent, Taipei up nine in the Overnight Watch’s file of that morning—gave the move back on Wednesday, in the wire account filed below and in the Dow Jones account filed below, and the two accounts do not agree on the size of the fall. Against the reversal stand two settled items: Dell Technologies rose 4.1 percent in after-hours trade in the wire account, on the record quarter it filed after Tuesday’s bell, and Wednesday’s American calendar is the fullest of the shortened week—the core PCE price index, durable goods, revised third-quarter product and jobless claims at 0830 Eastern, new-home sales at 1000 and the Beige Book at 1400, ahead of Thursday’s Thanksgiving close. In the Gulf, the Houthis claimed on Wednesday what Saudi attribution had assigned them on Tuesday, and added a refinery to the claim. In Ukraine, the air force counted 112 drones in the night. In the strait, Tehran counted two more tankers. In Moscow, the defence ministry counted nothing at all, into a fifth day.

What the night settled is Dell’s direction after hours, in the wire’s reading; the hearing dates for the ground stop, December 1 and December 2; Ukraine’s count of the night’s drones, as the air force files it; and the strait’s Tuesday, corrected by its own counter to four crossings. What it left open is the tariff file’s contents and timing; Wednesday’s inflation print and the session that trades on it; the fires the Houthis claim at Ras Tanura; the tankers Tehran names by number and never by name; and the ministry’s word on the Merkury.

Asia at Dawn: The Rally Returned in a Morning, and a Tariff File Reopened Behind It

The reversal’s direction is in every account in the file; its depth is not. The broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 2.3 percent in the wire account’s early reading and down 3.2 percent in the later form of the same wire copy carried in the file. South Korea fell as much as 5.3 percent in the early reading, 5.9 percent in the Dow Jones update and 6.2 percent in the Bloomberg-figures account filed below. Taiwan fell 5.1 percent at its worst in the early reading, 8.6 percent at its worst in the later wire form, 6.0 percent in the Dow Jones update and 4.8 percent in the Bloomberg-figures account. Japan’s Nikkei fell as much as 2.9 percent in the wire, 2.9 percent in the Dow Jones update and 2.8 percent in the Bloomberg figures. The names under the indexes agree better than the indexes do: SK Hynix down 9.8 percent in one account and 11.1 percent in another, Samsung Electronics down 9.1 percent and 9.9 percent, Kioxia down more than 10 percent in Tokyo in one and 14.2 percent in the other, and the Korea Exchange briefly suspended trading on Kospi constituents after futures fell more than 5 percent, in the Dow Jones account. Hong Kong is the file’s open disagreement: the Hang Seng down 0.25 percent in the update, down 0.7 percent in the Bloomberg figures, and up 1.0 percent in the earlier Dow Jones form.

Two causes are named in the accounts, and the desk prints both as the accounts give them. The first is the trade itself: relief at Mr. Huang’s reinstatement waned and doubts about the artificial-intelligence build-out returned, six sessions after Anthropic’s debut and one day after its first close under its offering price. The second is a file reopened in Washington: the Trade Representative’s office is preparing to release the findings of a months-long investigation into alleged excess industrial capacity and industrial subsidies among 16 major trading partners, including China and the European Union, three people with knowledge of the matter told the wire, and the findings could pave the way for new tariff measures. The Trade Representative, Jamieson Greer, is expected to unveil the results as soon as this week, in the Journal’s reporting as carried in the Dow Jones account, with the warning that the timing could change. An analyst note in the same account puts the possible effect plainly: the proposed duties could lift the effective tariff rate back toward the levels seen before February, when the Supreme Court ruled the president’s global tariffs illegal. No findings have been released at the stamp, and no rate is named in any account in the file. Settled: the selling, and the file’s existence as reported. Open: the findings, their date, and their numbers.

Against the selling, the night carried one verdict the Midnight Watch had to leave split. Dell Technologies, which filed record fiscal third-quarter revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103 percent, and adjusted earnings of $9.45 a share against estimates near $6.60 after Tuesday’s bell, in the company’s filing filed below, rose 4.1 percent in after-hours trading, in the wire account. The midnight file carried one account with Dell rallying in extended trading and a second with it fallen further overnight; the wire’s Wednesday reading supports the first. The desk records the direction as the wire files it and notes that the stock had fallen nearly 12 percent in Tuesday’s session before either reading was taken. Anthropic’s position did not change in the night: the close at $81.91, down 6.5 percent and under the $83 offering price, stands as the closing account filed below printed it.

Washington at Dawn: An Inflation Print at 0830, a Stake Still a Sentence, and Two Hearing Dates Set

Wednesday is the week’s whole calendar in one morning, in the week-ahead account filed below and in the overnight futures account filed below: the October core PCE price index at 0830 Eastern, expected to rise 3.2 percent from a year earlier and described in both accounts as the final inflation reading before the Federal Reserve’s December 8-9 meeting, at which the futures markets have priced a further increase in rates; durable goods orders, the second estimate of third-quarter product and jobless claims in the same hour; new-home sales at 1000; and the Beige Book at 1400. Thursday the markets are closed for Thanksgiving and Friday’s session ends at 1300, so whatever position Wednesday’s print forces must be carried across a closed day. The futures at the stamp stand lower in every reading in the file, S&P 500 futures down 0.3 percent in the wire’s early reading and down 0.9 percent in the Bloomberg-figures account, Nasdaq-100 futures down 0.8 percent in the futures account and down 1.6 percent in the Bloomberg figures.

The President’s sentence on a government stake in Nvidia stands where the Midnight Watch left it—“It’s probably not too late,” given to the New York Post—with no proposal, price or structure added in the night’s file. The Journal’s reporting, carried in the Dow Jones account, adds the surrounding fact that the President pushed for Mr. Huang’s reappointment as Nvidia’s chief executive, raising the question the account itself phrases as the government’s role in the AI expansion. Mr. Huang’s December dates stand: the transcribed interview on December 1, his general counsel on December 2, and the Senate Banking Committee hearing on December 3.

The ground stop’s file gained its dates in the night. Secretary Duffy will testify on December 2 before the Senate Commerce aviation subcommittee, on the November 13 stop and on his request for $50 billion for air traffic control and airport modernization—raised from $30 billion after the incident, in the hearing account filed below—and Administrator Bedford will appear before a House panel on December 1. The account puts the stop’s cost at more than 18,000 cancelled flights and 1.5 million travellers disrupted, and names it the longest nationwide stop since September 11, 2001. The laboratory finding stands as the investigation account filed below reported it: an overlooked router setting, a report in preparation, investigators 90 percent sure no nefarious actor caused the failure. The formal findings stand unreleased at the stamp, and the account notes there is no indication when the agency will release them. Settled: the dates, and the size of the ask. Open: the report.

Riyadh at Dawn: The Claim Arrives, and It Is Larger Than the Strike

At midnight the Riyadh file stood on Saudi attribution: the authorities assigned Tuesday’s second strike on the Public Investment Fund tower to Yemen’s Houthi fighters, the coalition promised a decisive response, and no claim had been issued by 1600 GMT. In the night the claim arrived, and it is larger than the strike it answers for. The Houthis said on Wednesday they had attacked the Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh’s financial district, in the claim account filed below; their spokesman, Yahya Saree, said the refinery attack caused fires and that the financial district was attacked in three phases. The coalition’s Wednesday word is narrower and different in kind: air defences intercepted and destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura, in the Eastern Province. No Saudi account in the file confirms a fire at the refinery, and no account in the file describes damage at Ras Tanura beyond the interceptions the coalition reports.

Tuesday’s strike itself stands as the midnight file printed it: 11 wounded in the second hit in less than a week on the capital’s tallest tower, two Saudis, two Indians, three Nepalese and four Egyptians, in the casualty account filed below, with the wire noting it could not determine when the Civil Defence photograph was taken or the full extent of the damage. What the night changes is the shape of the exchange: a tower struck twice now stands beside a refinery claimed struck and defended in the same Wednesday statements, and the response the coalition promised on Tuesday has not been described in any account in the file at the stamp. Settled: the claim, as a claim, and the four interceptions, as the coalition files them. Open: the refinery’s state, and the response.

Ukraine at Dawn: A Hundred and Twelve Drones Counted in the Night

Ukraine’s night is filed in two layers, and the desk keeps them separate. The first layer is Tuesday night’s, carried at midnight: two dead in the Odesa region, including a boy of 17 in one account, three injured there, and two injured in Kyiv where a fire was set in a multi-storey building, in the wire account filed below and in the strikes account filed below. The second layer is the count of the night just ended, filed by the air force and carried in the air-force account filed below: 112 strike drones launched in the night of November 25, 66 of them jet-powered, from five sites in Russia and one in Crimea; 88 shot down or suppressed by 0800 Kyiv time, 47 of those jet-powered; hits recorded at 18 locations and debris at 13 more. The account gives no casualty figure for the night’s attack, and no Russian statement on either night’s strikes stands in the file at the stamp. Dymer’s toll stands at 12, its last figure unchanged in the night. Settled: the air force’s arithmetic, as filed. Open: what the 18 locations were, and what they cost.

The Strait at Dawn: Two More Tankers by Tehran’s Count, None by the Counter’s

Tehran’s count rose again in the night, on the same terms as every rise before it. Two oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines while attempting an unauthorized route, off the southern and eastern coasts of the strait, in the Guards’ Navy statement carried in the Tehran account filed below and in the second form of the statement filed below; the tankers had their navigation and positioning systems switched off, the statement says, and the warning to ships sailing dark was repeated. The same statement’s frame reaches backward: four other tankers exploded and caught fire in the preceding hours, which is Tuesday’s four as Tehran announced them. No vessel is named, no crew is accounted for, and Central Command has filed no answer at the stamp.

The visible counter’s night moved in the opposite direction: it corrected its own Tuesday. Four commercial ships crossed on November 24, one inbound and three outbound, one of them a tanker, the last the general cargo ship Palau inbound at 2127 UTC, in the strait count filed below—one more crossing than the three the Midnight Watch printed from the same counter, the correction stated here in the open. The seven days stand at 49 crossings, about 8 percent of the normal rate, and on Wednesday no ship had crossed by 0637 UTC, which is 0137 Eastern, inside this watch’s collection. The second instrument’s wider count, 27 ships in the 24 hours to 0001 UTC, stands as the midnight file printed it. Settled: Tuesday’s four, in the one instrument, and Wednesday’s two, in Tehran’s statements as statements. Open, as it has been open all week: the tankers themselves.

Libya at Dawn: The Ministry Silent Into a Fifth Day, and Kyiv’s Answer Filed Under Article 51

The Benghazi file’s night adds a legal sentence and nothing from the ministry the Kremlin named. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, Heorhii Tykhyi, said on November 24 that the strikes on the Merkury and the second ship were an exercise of Ukraine’s right of self-defence under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, and that Russian warships, cargo ships carrying military equipment and shadow-fleet tankers are legitimate targets, in the Benghazi account filed below. The same account records the eastern command’s word that two Libyan naval personnel died on November 24 of wounds from the November 22 attack, and the eastern government’s head naming the attack in his own terms. The imagery account, in the basing account filed below, stands as it stood: satellite imagery shows the corvette capsized with only her forward bow above water, where she had stopped to refuel and resupply under the cooperation agreement while escorting Russian cargo ships. Russia’s defence ministry had issued no statement on the Merkury by the time of the account’s November 25 update—not a confirmation, not a denial, not a list of her crew—and the silence the Midnight Watch counted into a fourth day now runs into its fifth. Settled: Kyiv’s legal position, stated in its spokesman’s words. Open: the ministry’s word, the crew’s full fate, and the joint inquiry’s answer.

The Cocked Hat

Where the overnight bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On Asia’s fall: the broad index down 2.3 percent early and 3.2 percent in the later wire form; Seoul down 5.3, 5.9 and 6.2 percent in three accounts; Taiwan down 4.8, 5.1 at its early worst, 6.0 and 8.6 at its later worst in four. On Hong Kong: down 0.25 percent, down 0.7 percent, and up 1.0 percent, in three accounts of the same morning. On Tuesday in the strait: four crossings in the counter’s corrected count, three in the count the Midnight Watch printed from the same counter before the correction, 27 ships in the monitor’s wider instrument, and four tankers claimed on mines in Tehran’s statements with none named. On Ras Tanura: fires claimed by the party that says it struck, and four drones destroyed by the defences of the party that owns the refinery, with no damage account from either. On Dell’s night, the triangle of the midnight file is closed by the wire’s 4.1 percent rise, and the desk closes it in the open. Inside the triangle is where the overnight honestly stands. The Midday Watch collects at 1200.

The Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the refinery attack caused fires and that the group had attacked the financial district in three phases. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier on Wednesday that air defences had intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province. Saudi civil defence said 11 people were wounded on Tuesday in a strike on a tower in Riyadh’s financial district, the second strike on the same tower in less than a week; the first, on November 19, damaged the building but caused no injuries.

 SubjectiveThe Business Standard, carrying Reuters—11 injured in second suspected Houthi strike on Riyadh’s tallest tower in daysAt least 11 people were injured when Yemen’s Houthi fighters struck the tallest skyscraper in Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh, on Tuesday, November 24, marking the second attack on the landmark building in less than a week. Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence reported the injuries and posted a picture of the tower, which houses the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund. The image showed damage to the building’s facade about halfway up, similar to the impact of a strike on the same tower on November 19, which caused damage but no injuries. Reuters could not immediately determine when the latest image was taken or the full extent of the damage from Tuesday’s strike. The Saudi-led coalition said a skyscraper in Riyadh’s financial district had been targeted.

 SubjectiveReuters—Russian strike kills two people in Ukraine’s Odesa region, governor saysA Russian strike killed two people and injured three more, including a child, in Ukraine’s Black Sea region of Odesa late on Tuesday, hitting cars and private and industrial buildings, Governor Oleh Kiper said on Telegram. Russian forces also attacked Kyiv with drones late on Tuesday, setting a fire in a multi-storey apartment building and injuring two people, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The account notes that the reports could not be independently verified and that Russia and Ukraine deny deliberately targeting civilians.

 SubjectiveAntikor, carrying the Air Force—Russia attacked Ukraine with 112 drones: air defence shot down 88, hits recorded at 18 locationsIn the night of November 25, Russia attacked Ukraine with 112 Shahed-type strike drones, 66 of them jet-powered, launched from Orel, Millerovo, Kursk, Shatalovo and Primorsko-Akhtarsk in Russia and from Gvardiyske in Crimea, in the Air Force’s account as carried. According to preliminary data, as of 0800 air defence shot down or suppressed 88 of the drones, 47 of them jet-powered. Hits by enemy air attack means were recorded at 18 locations, and the fall of downed drones, or debris, at 13 locations.

 SubjectiveParticle News—Russian Drone Strikes Kill 12 in Dymer and Two in Odesa, Injure Residents in KyivJet-powered drone strikes on Tuesday, November 24, hit Odesa Oblast and Kyiv, killing two people in Odesa, including a 17-year-old, and injuring three, and striking outside a 16-storey building in Kyiv, starting fires and injuring two residents. The account also carries Dymer’s confirmed toll of 12, after the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble died in hospital.

 SubjectivePress TV—Two oil tankers catch fire after hitting naval mines in Strait of Hormuz: IRGCThe Guards’ Navy says two oil tankers have exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines while attempting to pass through an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz, in a statement released on Wednesday. The incidents occurred off the southern and eastern coasts of the waterway, causing explosions and fires in the vessels’ engine rooms; the tankers had attempted to cross covertly, the statement said. The Navy issued a fresh warning to vessels operating with their navigation and positioning systems switched off. The incident follows a series of similar explosions over the preceding hours, in which four other oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the strait.

 SubjectiveHatha Alyoum—IRGC Navy says two ‘violating’ oil tankers hit naval mine in Hormuz StraitIran’s Guards’ Navy said that two offending oil tankers on the southern and eastern coasts of the Strait of Hormuz suffered explosions. The tankers, believing they were secretly trying to pass through the route the statement calls fake, were prevented from passing by naval mines, causing a massive explosion and fire, the statement said. It warned crews of ships with navigation and positioning systems turned off not to let the statements of American officials lead them to the explosion and fire of naval mines.

 SubjectiveHormuz.now—Strait of Hormuz News Today: Latest Status Update, 25 November 2026On 25 November 2026, no AIS-visible commercial ship had crossed the Strait of Hormuz yet, as of 0637 UTC. Yesterday, on 24 November, four commercial ships crossed, one inbound and three outbound, one of them a tanker, the most recent the general cargo ship Palau, inbound into the Gulf, at 2127 UTC. The last seven days stand at 49 crossings, 33 inbound and 16 outbound, including 16 tankers and two LNG or LPG carriers, a seven-day average of 7.0 a day, about 8 percent of normal. The status stands restricted, severely restricted, in this status since October 19. Ships are crossing under United States naval coordination; Iran claims control and requires transit permits; the official threat level is severe.

 SubjectiveCNN—FAA probe zeroes in on culprit of nationwide ground stop, but agency still faces tough questionsInvestigators into the November 13 nationwide ground stop have recreated the failure in a laboratory and believe they have found the culprit, according to a source familiar with the investigation: an overlooked router setting affected how the new router at the remote Arkansas site interfaced with decades-old routers being decommissioned, and software updates are believed necessary to prevent a repeat. The investigators are preparing a report; the source said investigators are 90 percent sure the disruption was not caused by nefarious actors, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation and other national security representatives took part. Administrator Bryan Bedford and Secretary Sean Duffy are set to appear at hearings next week. The account also carries the dispute over oversight: the technicians’ union says maintenance coordination has been reduced to four liaisons nationwide and a layer of agency review eliminated, and the agency’s statement says it performs continuous risk assessments and oversees the contractor through service performance monitoring, not field supervision.

 SubjectiveReuters, carried by 947 The Beast—US officials to testify before Congress on air travel ground stopTransportation Secretary Sean Duffy will testify next week before a Senate subcommittee to answer questions on the November 13 nationwide ground stop that led to more than 18,000 canceled flights and disrupted travel for 1.5 million Americans. Duffy will face questions on December 2 from the Senate Commerce aviation subcommittee on his request for $50 billion for air traffic control and airport modernization, the panel said on Tuesday. Administrator Bryan Bedford is separately set to appear before a House panel on December 1. Duffy had earlier asked for $30 billion, including $18 billion for airports, but raised the request to $50 billion after the incident, the longest nationwide ground stop since the September 11, 2001 attacks. Duffy has said a Juniper router produced by Hewlett Packard Enterprise, installed by L3Harris Technologies in a remote Arkansas facility, triggered the nearly five-hour stop. Testing has been ongoing on the router at a laboratory in Florida, and there is no indication when the agency will release findings.

 SubjectiveDefenceMENA—Ukraine Says Its Sea Drones Sank Russian Corvette Merkury in BenghaziUkraine says seven of its naval drones sank the Russian Navy corvette Merkury at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya before dawn on November 22 and hit a Russian cargo ship off the city later that day; Moscow has not confirmed the loss. In an update dated November 25, two members of the eastern-based Libyan National Army’s naval forces died on November 24 of wounds sustained in the attack, the General Command said; the eastern government’s head, Osama Hammad, said they died as a result of their injuries during the attack on the port of Benghazi. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi said on November 24 that the strikes were an exercise of Ukraine’s right to self-defence under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter and that Russian warships, cargo ships carrying military equipment and shadow-fleet tankers were legitimate targets. Russia’s Defence Ministry had still not commented on the Merkury by the time of the update.

 SubjectiveBattlePolicy—Merkury Sunk in Benghazi: Russia’s Libya Basing ProblemUkraine’s security service says a mother ship put seven naval drones in the water off Libya and they sank the Russian corvette Merkury at its berth on November 22. Vantor satellite imagery shows the Merkury capsized with only its forward bow above water. The Institute for the Study of War said the corvette had stopped for several days under a cooperation agreement with eastern Libya’s government, refuelling and resupplying while it escorted Russian cargo ships. Russia’s Defence Ministry has not commented. The Kremlin spokesman warned of escalation over a separate attack in the Baltic.

### Tuesday Closes With the Futures Down and Nvidia Down Again in Late Trade, Dell's Record Quarter Beaten in the Session and Disputed After It, Anthropic Under Its Offering Price, a Second Strike on Riyadh's Tallest Tower, and New Dead in Odesa and Kyiv While Moscow Files No Word on the Merkury Into a Fourth Day

Filed as: Edition No. 88 — The Midnight Watch · 2026-11-25T00:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-25-midnight-watch.html

The Midnight File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Tuesday Closes With the Futures Down and Nvidia Down Again in Late Trade, Dell’s Record Quarter Beaten in the Session and Disputed After It, Anthropic Under Its Offering Price, a Second Strike on Riyadh’s Tallest Tower, and New Dead in Odesa and Kyiv While Moscow Files No Word on the Merkury Into a Fourth Day

 The last entry of the day, filed before the log turns: a rally giving back its second day in the futures; a record quarter the session sold and the night argued over; a new stock under its offering price; a president weighing a government stake in the company at the center of it all; a culprit found in a laboratory and a report not yet written; a tower struck twice in a week; and two counts—of tankers and of crossings—that still do not meet.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 0000 ET, Wednesday, November 25, 2026. This edition closes the day continued in Edition No. 87, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Tuesday, in Edition No. 86, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Tuesday, in Edition No. 85, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 on Tuesday, and in Edition No. 84, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 on Tuesday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the midnight figures differ from the evening figures, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Midnight in Brief: What Tuesday Settled, What It Left Open

Tuesday settled its close, its last Senate race, and the second full day of the Huang restoration—and in the hours after the bell it unsettled the first of those: the futures are down at the stamp, the week’s largest new stock closed under its offering price, and the President told a newspaper it is probably not too late for his government to take a stake in Nvidia. The futures stand lower in both late readings in the file—Nasdaq-100 futures down 0.8 percent in the overnight account filed below and down 1.17 percent at 2151 Eastern in the late account filed below—with Nvidia down 2 percent in late trade. After the bell Dell Technologies filed a record quarter, and Anthropic closed at $81.91, below its $83 offering price for the first time. In Washington, investigators into the November 13 ground stop have a culprit in a laboratory and a report in preparation, and the formal findings stand unreleased. In Ukraine, late strikes killed two in the Odesa region and injured two in Kyiv. In Riyadh, a drone struck the Public Investment Fund tower a second time in a week and wounded 11.

What Tuesday settled is the close; Dell’s quarter and its raised year; Anthropic’s first close under its offering price; Dymer’s twelve, with two more of the dead now named; and the strait’s Tuesday at three crossings in the visible counter. What it left open is Wednesday’s session and the inflation print before it; whether a government stake in Nvidia is an idea or a proposal; the ground stop’s unwritten report; the response Riyadh promised; Tehran’s unnamed tankers; and the defence ministry’s word on the Merkury, unissued into a fourth day.

The Markets at Midnight: The Futures Down, and a Record Quarter the Night Cannot Agree On

The close stands as the Evening Watch printed it, with one table in the late file differing in its last figures: the Dow up 0.85 percent, the S&P 500 down 0.50 percent and the Nasdaq Composite down 1.48 percent in both tellings, the Dow’s level at 50,026.46 in the evening’s closing account and at 50,018.70 in the late account’s table. The night’s direction is not in dispute: the futures fell in every reading, and crude fell more than 1 percent overnight after settling up 2.35 percent at $82.05. Wednesday is the week’s fullest morning before Thursday’s Thanksgiving close: durable goods, revised third-quarter product and jobless claims at 0830 Eastern, and new-home sales and the PCE price index at 1000, with the core PCE expected to rise 3.2 percent from a year earlier, in the overnight account. Settled: the close and the calendar. Open: the print, and the session that trades on it.

The after-hours report was Dell’s, and it is HPE’s Monday in mirror: the numbers beat, and the stock’s night is argued. Dell filed record fiscal third-quarter revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103 percent, against estimates of $49.32 billion; adjusted earnings of $9.45 a share, up 265 percent, against estimates near $6.60; infrastructure revenue of $42.0 billion, up 198 percent, with AI server revenue of $22.0 billion, up 291 percent; and a full-year guide raised to $202 billion from $192 billion, in the company’s release and in the earnings account filed below. The session had sold the stock nearly 12 percent in the chip decline. After the bell, one account carries Dell rallying in extended trading, in the results account filed below, and the late futures account carries it fallen further overnight. The desk prints both readings and settles neither; the quarter itself is settled, in the filing.

The day’s other verdict came at the close, on the newest large stock in the market. Anthropic, which opened on November 19 at $111.50 against an $83 offering price in the largest offering on record, traded as low as $75.61 on Tuesday and closed at $81.91, down 6.5 percent—its first close below the price at which the public bought it, in the closing account filed below. Its capitalization touched $999.5 billion in the session, below $1 trillion for the first time. Monday’s rally did not lift this stock; Tuesday’s decline took it under water, six sessions after its debut.

Washington at Midnight: A Stake Weighed in the Open, and the President’s Own Holding in the File

The evening’s Washington news is a sentence of the President’s, given to the New York Post and carried in the overnight account: on a United States government equity stake in Nvidia, “I thought about it. I said, ‘You know, maybe I should do it,’ but I didn’t bring it up at this point. It’s probably not too late.” He noted that Intel handed over a stake of near 10 percent to the United States. In the stake account filed below, he is further reported as saying he would pardon Mr. Huang if it became necessary, and that he expects no pardon will be needed. No proposal has been made to the company in any account in the file; the size, structure and purpose of a stake are nowhere stated. Mr. Huang’s December dates stand: the transcribed interview on December 1, his general counsel on December 2, and the Senate Banking Committee hearing on December 3.

The President’s own position in the stock is also in the day’s file, in ranges, as the disclosure law files it. His Nvidia holding may have gained as much as $15 million in Monday’s rise, an upper bound computed from disclosures filed November 5 showing between 32,000 and 370,000 shares held as of September 30, in the holdings account filed below; the forms do not cover October and November trades, and the exact gain cannot be determined from them. A second account, in the stake-and-holding account filed below, counts at least 103 purchases or sales of the stock in the President’s second term. The White House statement carried in both accounts is the same: the portfolio is independently managed through model portfolios, and neither the President nor his family can direct it. Settled: the words, and the ranges. Open: everything a stake would require—a proposal, a price, and a board’s answer.

The Ground Stop at Midnight: A Culprit Recreated in a Laboratory, and the Findings Still Unreleased

The ground stop’s file moved on Tuesday for the first time since the industry’s $30 billion ask on Monday, and it moved by leak rather than by release. Investigators have recreated the November 13 failure in a laboratory and believe they have found the culprit, according to a source familiar with the investigation in the investigation account above: an overlooked router setting, affecting how the new router at the remote Arkansas site interfaced with the decades-old routers being decommissioned, with software updates believed necessary to prevent a repeat. The investigators are preparing a report, and the source put them at 90 percent sure the disruption was not caused by nefarious actors. The formal findings—the release the administrator expected by last Friday and the Senate Commerce Democrats asked after for Monday—stand unreleased at the stamp, and the desk files the laboratory account as an account, not as the findings. Administrator Bedford and Secretary Duffy are set to appear at hearings next week.

The argument beneath the finding is also in the account, in both voices. The technicians’ union holds that the failed maintenance was coordinated under a system reduced to four liaisons nationwide and that a layer of agency review was eliminated to speed the work. The agency’s statement holds that it performs continuous risk assessments and oversees the contractor, which owns the infrastructure, through performance monitoring rather than field supervision. The account closes with a precedent: on November 19, 2009, a misconfigured router in Los Angeles blocked about 75 percent of the same network. Settled: a mechanism, in a laboratory, on a source’s word. Open: the report, the patches, and the hearings.

Ukraine at Midnight: Dymer’s Twelve Named Further, and New Strikes in Odesa and Kyiv

At midnight Dymer’s file gains names rather than numbers. The toll stands at 12, the twelfth being Valentyna, seventy-nine, pulled alive on November 23 after nearly a day under the rubble and dead in hospital on November 24, in the toll account filed below, which spells the settlement Dymery. Two more of the dead are now identified in print: Kateryna Bovtunenko, 33, and her daughter Kira, 11, the youngest victim of the strike, in the running file filed below, in reporting credited to Ukrainska Pravda. The boy Davyd, seven, stands as the file’s survivor.

The night’s new file is south and in the capital. Late on Tuesday a Russian strike in the Odesa region killed two people and injured three, including a child, hitting cars and private and industrial buildings, Governor Oleh Kiper said on Telegram, in the wire account above; a second account, in the strikes account filed below, names the weapons as jet-powered drones and one of the dead as a boy of 17. In Kyiv, drones attacked late on Tuesday, a fire was set in a multi-storey apartment building—a 16-storey building, struck outside, in the strikes account—and two people were injured, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, in the wire account, which notes the reports could not be independently verified. No Russian statement on the night’s strikes stands in the file at the stamp. Settled: the governor’s and the mayor’s figures, as filed. Open: the night’s full count, which the Overnight Watch will take at 0400.

Riyadh at Midnight: The Tallest Tower Struck a Second Time in a Week, Eleven Wounded, and a Response Promised

Riyadh’s file is a repetition, and the repetition is the news. On Tuesday a drone struck the tallest tower in the Saudi capital—the 385-metre headquarters of the Public Investment Fund in the King Abdullah Financial District—for the second time in less than a week, wounding at least 11 people, Saudi Civil Defense reported, in the Riyadh account above. The injured were two Saudis, two Indians, three Nepalese and four Egyptians, in the casualty account filed below. The first strike, on November 19, damaged the same tower and injured no one. The Saudi-led coalition said the attack was carried out with a drone and that it would respond decisively to the deliberate targeting of civilians and civilian property. Attribution in the file is Saudi: the authorities attribute the strike to Yemen’s Houthi fighters, and in the casualty account the Houthis had issued no claim by 1600 GMT on Tuesday. Settled: the strike, the count of the wounded, and the promise of a response. Open: the response itself, and any word from the party named as the striker.

The Strait at Midnight: Three Crossings for Tuesday, and Tehran’s Count at Four for the Day, Still Without a Name

Tuesday’s visible count is the lowest full day the counter has filed this month. Three commercial ships crossed on 24 November, none inbound and three outbound, one of them a tanker, the last the bulk carrier Guan Yuan Fu Xing at 1411 UTC, and the seven days stand at 51 crossings, in the strait count filed below. The second instrument counts 27 ships in the 24 hours to 0001 UTC on 25 November, 12 in and 15 out, with tankers carrying an estimated 2.10 million barrels out, in the monitor account filed below. Against those counts, Tehran’s Tuesday statements raised its own. Four oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines on Tuesday, in the statements of the Guards’ Navy and the Armed Forces’ Navy carried in the Tehran account filed below, and two further tankers were turned back to the Gulf after a radio warning from the Traffic Control Centre. The Guards’ wider count, in the two-day account filed below, stands at six tankers caught fire and sunk on Sunday and Monday. No vessel is named in any of it; Central Command has filed no answer at the stamp; and the British maritime office’s standing report of the week remains projectiles, not mines—three vessels struck on Sunday, all crews accounted for, all continuing their transits. Settled: Tuesday’s three, in the one instrument, and Tehran’s announcements, as announcements. Open: the tankers themselves.

Libya at Midnight: No Word From the Ministry Into a Fourth Day, and the Log Counts the Hull

The Benghazi file closes Tuesday where it has stood since Monday morning: the Russian defence ministry, to which the Kremlin referred every question, had issued no statement on the Merkury by the stamp—not a confirmation, not a denial, not a list of her crew—and the silence the Overnight Watch counted at three days at 0400 now runs into its fourth calendar day. What the day added is accounting and one detail from the water. A naval events log counts the Merkury as the 25th Russian hull recorded as lost since February 24, 2022, and the first outside the Black Sea basin, in the log account filed below. In the Benghazi account filed below, satellite images showed the corvette submerged against the dock; a Moscow channel with links to the military is reported as saying her guns destroyed four of the seven attacking drones and two got through; and two Libyan soldiers died of injuries sustained in the attack. Kyiv’s claim stands unamended, the second ship stands as the Angara in Kyiv’s word, and Libya’s two governments stand as they stood: the east investigating with Russia, the west condemning. Settled: the log’s count of the hull. Open: the ministry’s word, the crew’s full fate, and the inquiry’s answer.

The Cocked Hat

Where the midnight bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On the futures: down 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8 percent in the overnight account; down 0.33, 0.65 and 1.17 percent at 2151 Eastern in the late account—two readings an hour apart, in one direction. On the Dow’s close: 50,026.46 in the evening’s closing account, 50,018.70 in the late account’s table, the gain 0.85 percent in both. On Dell after hours: a rally in extended trading in one account, and a further fall overnight in the late futures account, against the same record quarter in the filing. On Anthropic’s fall: 6.5 percent at the close in three accounts, 9 percent in a fourth’s midday reading. On Tuesday in the strait: three crossings in the visible counter, 27 ships in the monitor’s wider 24 hours, and four tankers claimed on mines in Tehran’s statements with none named. On the Guards’ two days: six tankers burned and sunk on Sunday and Monday in the two-day account, against three claimed for Monday in Monday’s own statements. On the settlement the desk has spelled Dymer all week: Dymery, in the Ukrainian account as rendered in English. Inside the triangle is where the midnight honestly stands, and the log turns on it. The Overnight Watch collects at 0400.

 The Clippings Filed With This Edition

 Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 24 items.

Administrator Bryan Bedford and Secretary Sean Duffy are set to appear at hearings next week. The account also carries the dispute over oversight: the technicians’ union says maintenance coordination has been reduced to four liaisons nationwide and a layer of agency review eliminated, and the agency’s statement says it performs continuous risk assessments and oversees the contractor through service performance monitoring, not field supervision.

 SubjectiveReuters — Russian strike kills two people in Ukraine’s Odesa region, governor saysA Russian strike killed two people and injured three more, including a child, in Ukraine’s Black Sea region of Odesa late on Tuesday, hitting cars and private and industrial buildings, Governor Oleh Kiper said on Telegram. Russian forces also attacked Kyiv with drones late on Tuesday, setting a fire in a multi-storey apartment building and injuring two people, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The account notes that the reports could not be independently verified and that Russia and Ukraine deny deliberately targeting civilians.

 SubjectiveParticle News — Russian Drone Strikes Kill 12 in Dymer and Two in Odesa, Injure Residents in KyivJet-powered drone strikes on Tuesday, November 24, hit Odesa Oblast and Kyiv, killing two people in Odesa, including a 17-year-old, and injuring three, and striking outside a 16-storey building in Kyiv, starting fires and injuring two residents. The account also carries Dymer’s confirmed toll of 12, after the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble died in hospital.

 SubjectiveHromadske, carried at h.ua — Woman rescued from rubble after Russian drone strike on Dymery dies, raising death toll to 12A 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble of a five-story residential building in the settlement spelled Dymery in this account died in hospital on November 24. Her death brought the fatalities from the November 22 drone strike to 12, including an 11-year-old girl. A seven-year-old boy, Davyd, was rescued alive.

 SubjectiveThe Library Estate — Russian Drone Destroys Five-Storey Apartment Block in Dymer; Rescuers Search Rubble for People Still Trapped, with updatesA running file on the November 22 strike on Dymer, updated through November 24. Its Tuesday update records that the death toll rose to 12, citing Governor Tymur Tkachenko: the 79-year-old woman rescued alive at 0328 on November 23 died in hospital. A further update the same day identifies two of those killed as Kateryna Bovtunenko, 33, and her 11-year-old daughter, Kira, the youngest victim of the strike, in reporting credited to Ukrainska Pravda.

 SubjectiveReuters, carried by KTWB — Houthis hit Riyadh’s tallest tower, 11 wounded, Saudi Civil Defense saysYemen’s Houthi fighters struck the tallest tower in Riyadh on Tuesday for the second time in less than a week, wounding at least 11 people, Saudi Civil Defense reported, posting a picture of the tower that houses the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund. The image showed damage about halfway up the facade, similar to the impact of the November 19 strike on the same tower, which caused damage and no injuries. The Saudi-led coalition said later on Tuesday that the attack was carried out with a drone and that it would respond decisively to the deliberate targeting of civilians and civilian property. The account notes that the wire could not immediately determine when the image was taken or the extent of the further damage.

 SubjectiveArchynewsy, carrying agency reporting — Houthi Drone Attack on Riyadh PIF Tower Injures 11, Second Strike in a WeekA drone strike on Riyadh’s financial district on Tuesday injured 11 people, the second hit on the capital’s tallest tower in less than a week, Saudi Civil Defence said. The tower is the 385-metre Public Investment Fund headquarters in the King Abdullah Financial District. The injured were two Saudi citizens, two Indians, three Nepalese and four Egyptians. The tower had been damaged in a strike on November 19 that caused no injuries. Saudi Arabia had not said how it would respond, and the Houthis had not claimed responsibility by 1600 GMT on November 24, in this account.

 SubjectiveDaily Prabhat, carrying ANI — Four oil tankers explode, catch fire after hitting naval mines in Hormuz: Iran’s NavyFour oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to statements of the Guards’ Navy and the Navy of the Armed Forces carried by the state broadcaster. One tanker struck a mine traveling through the strait earlier in the day and exploded east of the waterway; two other tankers were forced to return to the Persian Gulf after witnessing the explosion and receiving a radio warning from the Traffic Control Centre; and the Navy reported two tankers that had disabled their identification and navigation systems before entering a restricted area east of the strait and struck mines. The Guards’ Navy warned that traveling through unauthorized routes will result in explosions and fires. The account also carries the British maritime office’s report of three vessels struck by unidentified projectiles on Sunday while transiting eastbound, all crews accounted for and the vessels continuing their transits.

 SubjectiveFairsOnline — IRGC says six Hormuz tankers burned in two days after mine hitsTwo oil tankers exploded and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines, the Guards’ Navy said on Monday, in a statement carried by the Mehr agency. The Guards’ Navy says six oil tankers in total caught fire and sank in the strait on Sunday and Monday. The account says the two tankers transited under the direct guidance of United States officers and with the support of United States fighter jets, describes the incidents as measures against what it calls an illegal United States blockade, and says pollution from the explosions has spread across coastal areas and waters of the strait. The Guards did not name the vessels, their owners or their cargo. The account also carries the statement of Iran’s chief negotiator and parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, to Al Jazeera last week that navigation in the strait would never return to pre-war conditions.

 SubjectiveHormuz Now — Strait of Hormuz News Today: Latest Status Update (25 Nov 2026)On 25 November 2026, no identification-system-visible commercial ship had crossed the Strait of Hormuz yet, as of 0236 UTC. On 24 November 2026, three commercial ships crossed, none inbound and three outbound, one of them a tanker; the most recent was the bulk carrier Guan Yuan Fu Xing, outbound at 1411 UTC. The last seven days stand at 51 crossings, 32 inbound and 19 outbound, including 16 tankers and two liquefied-gas carriers, about 9 percent of the pre-crisis 84.8 a day, with the status severely restricted. The brief states that it counts ships visible on the identification system and misses the ships sailing dark.

 SubjectiveStrait of Hormuz Ship Monitor — Live Map: Ship Positions and Tanker TrafficIn the 24 hours to 0001 UTC on 25 November 2026, 27 ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz, 12 into the Gulf and 15 out of it, and tankers carried an estimated 2.10 million barrels of oil out through the strait. The monitor’s crossing table for 24 November lists, among others, the bulk carrier Guan Yuan Fu Xing outbound, the products tanker Jasmin inbound in its own timing, and the bulk carrier Erona outbound.

 SubjectiveThe Times — Putin’s ships burning off Libya shows how Ukraine war has gone globalUkrainian drone boats struck the corvette Merkuriy at her berth in Benghazi in the early hours of Sunday, and satellite images by morning showed the ship submerged and slumped against the dock. The security service said its uncrewed vessels reached their targets and struck both the Merkuriy and the second vessel, the MV Angara. A channel in Moscow with links to the military, Rybar, is reported as saying the Merkuriy’s guns destroyed four of the attacking drones and two got through. The account also records that two Libyan soldiers died of injuries sustained during the attack, and that Libya’s eastern prime minister, Osama Hammad, has asked the United Nations to investigate whether the drones were launched from western Libya.

 SubjectiveGlobalMilitary.net — Merkury, Sunk in Libya, Is the First of Russia’s 25 Logged Naval Losses Outside the Black Sea BasinThe corvette Merkury sank at her berth in Benghazi at dawn on November 22, 2026, after an explosion and a brief fire, in this account’s naval events log. The log counts the Merkury as the 25th Russian hull recorded as lost since February 24, 2022, and the first outside the Black Sea basin. Who sank the ship rests, so far, on statements from Kyiv: President Zelensky’s post of November 23 said Ukrainian forces attacked with seven naval drones, that the Merkury was sunk and the cargo ship Angara damaged. Ten Russian and Libyan crew members were injured in the wire reporting carried. The Kremlin said the Defence Ministry would provide information; the ministry had not commented, in this account.

### The Dow Closes Above 50,000 as the Nasdaq Falls on Nvidia's Retreat, Dymer's Toll Rises to Twelve, and Mr. Sullivan Concedes in Alaska While Poland Renews Its Push for American Troops

Filed as: Edition No. 87 — The Evening Watch · 2026-11-24T18:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-24-evening-watch.html

The Evening File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 The Dow Closes Above 50,000 as the Nasdaq Falls on Nvidia’s Retreat, Dymer’s Toll Rises to Twelve, and Mr. Sullivan Concedes in Alaska While Poland Renews Its Push for American Troops

 The evening file—the day’s developments whole, and the first considered responses from every side: a close that split in two, a confidence print from before the rally, a toll that rose by one in a hospital, a concession that closed the last Senate race, and two straits of the record—one in Poland, one at Hormuz—where the counts still do not agree.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1800 ET, Tuesday, November 24, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 86, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 today, from Edition No. 85, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 today, and from Edition No. 84, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the evening figures differ from the figures those editions carried, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Evening in Brief: A Close That Split, a Toll That Rose by One, and a Race That Closed

In brief: Wall Street closed split on Tuesday, the Dow above 50,000 for the close and the technology indexes down, as the stock that made Monday’s rally gave back part of it; the last uncalled Senate race of the midterms closed with a concession in Alaska; the toll in Dymer rose from eleven to twelve in a hospital; and on the two military files of the day—Poland and the Strait of Hormuz—the responses arrived while the underlying counts still did not agree. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 50,026.46, up 0.87 percent, the S&P 500 at 7,202.45, down 0.48 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite down about 1.5 percent, in the closing account and the market account filed below. Nvidia closed at $155.38, down 5.86 percent, after Monday’s gain of 31.48 percent to $165.05. In Alaska, the certified count stands at 144,583 votes for Mary Peltola and 132,022 for Dan S. Sullivan, in the state’s own report filed below, and Mr. Sullivan conceded on Tuesday. In Dymer, the woman of seventy-nine who was pulled alive from the rubble died in hospital, and the toll stands at twelve, in the updated account filed below. The desk takes the files in that order.

What the evening settled is the close, in full; the Alaska result, certified and conceded; Dymer’s new toll; and the calendar in Washington, where Mr. Huang’s December appearances stand confirmed in both parties’ tellings. What it left open is the rest: whether the tanker counts at Hormuz describe mines, projectiles, or the same ships counted twice; what Poland’s renewed request for American troops will produce; and whether Tuesday’s split close is a rotation or the start of a second slide, in a week shortened by Thanksgiving.

The Markets at the Close: The Dow Above 50,000, the Nasdaq Down, and Nvidia Down 5.86 Percent

The close completes the arc the Midday Watch left open at 1200, when the Dow stood up and the Nasdaq down in the morning figures. At the bell the split had widened and held. The Dow added 431.15 points in the closing account’s figures, to 50,026.46; another account puts the gain at more than 400 points, or 0.9 percent, and a third at 398 points, or 0.80 percent—the three accounts agree on direction and differ on the last figures, and the desk prints the closing account’s table as its table. The S&P 500 fell 34.72 points, or 0.48 percent, to 7,202.45, from Monday’s close at 7,237.17. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.5 percent in the market account and 1.48 percent in another; the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.98 percent to 26,216.64. Retailers helped the Dow ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, in the accounts filed below. The chip stocks fell together: Micron down 11.0 percent to $629.79 in the movers account, Intel among the most active names down, and Nvidia itself down 5.86 percent to $155.38 on volume of 379.27 million shares in the closing account. One account puts Nvidia’s fall at 8 percent; the price it prints in the other accounts, $155.38 against Monday’s $165.05, is a fall of 5.86 percent, and the desk follows the prices. Monday’s gain is not erased: at $155.38 the stock stands $29.85 above its Friday level before the reinstatement, on the figures in the file. Settled: the close, and its split. Open: Wednesday’s session, with the October PCE report and the Federal Reserve’s Beige Book ahead of Thursday’s Thanksgiving close.

The day’s economic print belongs to an earlier week. The Conference Board’s index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, from 91.9 in October, the highest since January 2025, in the wire account and the Board’s own release, both filed below. The release states its limit in its own lines: the survey closed November 17. The print therefore measures the country the week after the midterms, before the fall and Monday’s rally. More respondents said jobs were plentiful, at 30.8 percent against 26.2 percent in October, and year-ahead inflation expectations fell to 5.7 percent.

The Responses: Mr. Huang’s December Dates Stand, in Both Parties’ Tellings

The Evening Watch’s remit is the first considered responses, and on the Huang reinstatement they are now a calendar. Congressional committees have confirmed that Mr. Huang’s appearances will go ahead as scheduled, in the schedule account filed below, carrying CBS News: a transcribed interview on December 1 with the House Intelligence Committee, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on China; Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, on December 2; and a public hearing before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, with Mr. Huang as the sole witness, in the Journal’s account filed below. A House Intelligence Committee spokesperson is quoted that the reinstatement “changes nothing.” Representative Jim Himes is quoted: “We expect to see him on Capitol Hill next week.”

The criticism ran in both parties. Three Republican chairmen—Representatives Moolenaar, Crawford and Mast—said the board’s brief investigation does not erase the national security questions, and they remain committed to answers on the smuggling of Nvidia products. Senator Cotton said the controversy is the tip of the iceberg and is not resolved because Mr. Huang has his job back. Senator Warren said the administration needs to explain what input was given and by whom; Senator Schumer said Democrats will use their full power to investigate; Representative Jeffries called the decision indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible. President Trump’s words stand in the earlier editions: that he convinced the board. No finding by any committee is in the file. The questions are scheduled; the answers are not yet given.

Poland: A Drone Called Intentional, an AWACS Authorized, and a Renewed Request for American Troops

Poland’s file gained its response on Tuesday. Warsaw renewed its push for a permanent United States military presence, in the diplomatic account filed below, following two incursions in four days. Poland’s charg&eacute; d’affaires in Washington, Bogdan Klich, briefed American officials on Tuesday and discussed the permanent deployment question again. The Monday night incident stands as the midday file printed it: the Operational Command said a drone had briefly violated Poland’s airspace; Deputy Defence Minister Zalewski treated the breach as intentional; and Deputy Minister Wziatek said it was a Russian surveillance drone over a populated area, where shooting it down could have caused damage from falling debris, in the wire account carried by Devdiscourse filed below. The shootdown had been authorized and was held. The alliance’s answer stands as authorized on Monday: a forward AWACS deployment, in the deployment account filed below. No Russian statement on the drone is in the file. Settled: Warsaw’s request, restated. Open: Washington’s answer.

The Strait: Two, Three and Four Tankers in Tehran’s Own Counts, No Vessel Named, and Oil Up $2.03 at the Settlement

The Strait file did not settle on Tuesday; it widened. Iran’s Army navy said two oil tankers struck mines and caught fire early on Tuesday east of the Strait of Hormuz, after entering a restricted area with their identification and navigation systems disabled, in the army statement account filed below. The Guards’ navy said a further tanker struck a mine early on Tuesday, bringing its own Tuesday figure to a fourth in the telling carried by the Tasnim-carried account filed below, against the three the Guards announced on Monday, in the Monday account filed below. A maritime roundup in the file counts five claimed over two days, three on Monday and two on Sunday, in the Marine Insight account. No statement in the file names a vessel, gives a crew count, or gives a casualty figure. The British maritime office, UKMTO, in the same accounts, links the week’s tanker incidents near Khasab to unidentified projectiles, not mines, and records crews accounted for and vessels continuing their transits in its delayed report of three vessels struck on Monday. United States Central Command had not responded to the Iranian claims in the accounts in the file, and no account in the file confirms a mine strike from a source outside Iran’s own services. Army Commander-in-Chief Amir Hatami’s words stand as printed at midday: the waterway will be more closed day by day, and it will not reopen until Iran’s seven conditions are met.

Oil traded the disagreement and settled higher. Brent touched $88.10 in the morning, its lowest since August, on rising supply, and settled at $91.40, up $2.03, or 2.27 percent; WTI touched $79.07 and settled at $82.05, up $1.88, or 2.35 percent, in the settlement account and the Journal’s futures file, both filed below. Wednesday brings the inventory figures, expected to show a third consecutive weekly increase in crude stocks.

Ukraine: Dymer’s Toll at Twelve, and a Night of 96 Drones in the Air Force’s Count

Dymer’s count changed in a hospital. The woman of seventy-nine, Valentyna in the earlier accounts, who was pulled alive from the rubble of the five-story building on Monday after about twenty-two hours, died in hospital, the Kyiv Regional Military Administration reported at 0806 on Tuesday, and the toll from the strike of November 22 stands at twelve, in the updated accounts filed below. The search ended on Monday with eleven dead, including a child of eleven, and a boy of seven pulled alive; those figures stand in the Monday account filed below, and the twelfth death is Tuesday’s addition to them, stated here in the open as the log requires. President Zelensky’s call, in the Monday account, was for tougher sanctions and export controls on the foreign-made engines and chips used in Shahed drones. The night file adds a new count without closing the old one: Ukraine’s air force reported an attack overnight into November 24 involving 96 drones, with hits at 13 locations and debris at two, and six people injured in Zhytomyr Oblast, in the Reflect account filed below. No Russian statement on Dymer is in the evening file.

Alaska: Certified at 50.14 Percent, Conceded on Tuesday, and the Senate at 56 Seats in the Accounts

The last Senate race of the 2026 midterms closed on Tuesday in the ordinary way: a certification, then a concession. Alaska certified its results on Monday, two days ahead of its target date in the accounts filed below. The state’s official summary, dated November 23, lists all 401 precincts reported and gives Mary Peltola 144,583 votes, 50.14 percent, against 132,022, 45.78 percent, for Senator Dan S. Sullivan; Gerald L. Heikes took 6,107 votes and Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. 4,767, a second Sullivan on the ballot whose votes, at 1.65 percent, are smaller than Ms. Peltola’s margin of 12,561. Because she cleared 50 percent of first choices, no ranked-choice tabulation was required. On Tuesday Mr. Sullivan conceded, in the words carried by the Juneau account filed below: he accepts the results certified by the Division of Elections. The Department of Justice, which had sued over the certification, said in a court filing that its lawsuit is now moot, in the concession account filed below, which counts the result as giving the Democrats 56 seats in the Senate that convenes on January 3. What was “Still Uncalled” on November 4 is now called, certified and conceded in full.

The Cocked Hat

Three bearings. On the close, the accounts agree on the split and on Nvidia’s price and differ in the last decimal of the Dow’s gain; one account’s 8 percent for Nvidia does not square with the $155.38 price the others print, and the desk followed the prices. On the strait, two, three, four and five tankers are all in print, with no name, no crew and no outside confirmation, against a British office that records projectiles and ships that continued their voyages; the desk prints the counts as claimed, and the disagreement as the fact. On confidence, the number is one number everywhere—103.3—and its date is its limit: a survey that closed November 17 cannot measure a rally that began November 23.

 SubjectiveThe Wall Street Journal — Jensen Huang’s Return to Nvidia Draws Heavy Fire From LawmakersCongressional Republicans sharply criticized Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s reinstatement, which President Trump helped engineer, while Democrats said they were preparing further investigations when they take control of Congress next year. The board said it had received input from senior levels of the United States government and is confident the reinstatement poses no national security risk. The Senate Banking Committee formally scheduled a public hearing at 10 a.m. Eastern on December 3 with Huang as the sole witness.

 SubjectiveBroadband Breakfast, carrying the Associated Press — Fury in Congress Over Huang’s Reinstatement as Lawmakers Move Forward With HearingsMembers of Congress responded with swift, bipartisan fury on Monday over the Nvidia board’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang at the behest of President Donald Trump. Senator Tim Scott announced that Huang will testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3. Senator Elizabeth Warren said the Trump administration needs to explain what role United States officials played in what she called a reckless decision.
